text:
Kavi: heads up — saw a p99 CPU spike on telemetry-consumer group for the last 10m, seems correlated with span ingest bursts. Anyone watching exporter behavior?
Maria: seeing same in prod, exporter queue length jumped ~4x around 20:10 UTC.
Josh: can you paste exporter backpressure metrics/logs? otel exporter default batch params might be amplifying latency.
Kavi: logging snippet: 
[exporter] flushed=512 spans duration=120ms backlog=3212 tls_handshake=45ms send_ms=85ms
node_cpu=92% p99_req_latency=600ms
Kavi: pattern: many small bursts, lots of short-lived grpc connections.
Inga: grpc + tls? short connections would explain handshake cost. Is keepalive/pooling enabled?
Kavi: yes grpc + TLS, region eu-west. SNI shows connection churn, lots of connection open/close.
Maria: I started a quick canary: reduce batch_size -> 128 and increase max_concurrent_requests -> 8, rolling to 10% now. Will report.
Josh: also try enabling persistent channels + preconnect. Short TLS lifecycles are expensive.
sre-bot: deploy: telemetry-exporter-config v2 rolled to 10% on prod - success
Kavi: quick results: CPU dropped ~30% on canary pods but p99 still spikes during heavy bursts. Timeline: 20:12 drop then 20:14 a spike.
Maria: local microbench: batch=512 99th=420ms; batch=128 99th=260ms. Smaller batches lower tail for bursts but increase per-span overhead.
Josh: long term: persistent grpc channels + client-side batching + preconnect; consider snappy compression for proto stream to cut TLS bytes.
Inga: compression currently off due to memory churn concerns — will evaluate memory vs bandwidth tradeoffs.
Kavi: another finding: retention compaction job runs concurrently on same nodes as exporters; node-level CPU contention likely exacerbates p99.
Maria: proposal: 1) move exporter pods to dedicated nodes (taint/toleration) 2) set batch_size=128 3) pre-warm TLS connections 4) enable snappy in eu-west only 5) add batch send_ms histograms and tls_handshake metric.
Josh: I'll PR the opentelemetry config changes and add client keepalive tuning. Also propose a canary that switches one tenant to HTTP/1.1 streaming for comparison.
Kavi: dashboards need updates: per-exporter queue_length, batch_size, send_ms p50/p95/p99, tls_handshake_ms, node co-scheduled job list. Who owns this?
Maria: I can take dashboards. Will add panels under telemetry -> exporters and link to the canary.
Inga: I'll instrument keepalive/preconnect and open a runtime PR to use pooled channels. I'll also add a guard to postpone compaction if exporter queue > X.
sre-bot: alert: exporter-send-ms p99 > 500ms triggered on telemetry-prod at 2026-03-20T20:23:41Z
Josh: consider adaptive batching: target_flush_ms = min(200, observed_99th/2) so batch window shrinks during heavy queues. Could be low-risk to prototype.
Kavi: for immediate mitigation we do maria's node separation + smaller batches + preconnect. Schedule a follow-up tomorrow to review canary metrics and test harness.
Maria: +1. I'll post config diffs and benchmark graphs once rollout at 50% completes.
Inga: noted. I'll also add a short doc in eng-platform describing exporter tuning knobs and why persistent channels matter.
Kavi: thanks — let's keep this thread for rollout notes and final dashboard links.
